original_content_blocks.content: Incident Report: BlockNote Integration - TypeScript and Runtime  Challenges    Date of Report: October 26, 2023 (Placeholder)  Prepared By: Gemini AI Assistant  Project: ThinkStash Knowledge Base Application  Affected Area: BlockNote Editor Integration, specifically custom image block with local upload  functionality.

items: The incident report details about the typescript type errors  •  The incident is frequent issues out influencing the image block  •  As the incident is hardly fixable, we propose to stick with current image block setting

Executive Summary:  A series of cascading TypeScript type errors and a subsequent runtime error (TypeError:  Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'requiredExtensions')) were encountered during  the development and enhancement of the BlockNote editor integration. The primary goal was to  add robust image handling, including local uploads and structured metadata storage, to the  default BlockNote "image" block. The root causes appear to be a combination of:  Breaking changes in Next.js 15 regarding API route parameter handling.  Known complexities and potential type definition quirks within the BlockNote library (v0.29.1,  then updated to v0.30.0), particularly concerning the distinction and assignability between  BlockSpec and BlockConfig.  The interaction of custom block property schemas with BlockNote's internal mechanisms for  schema creation and editor initialization.  Significant effort has been made to refactor schema definitions and apply community- recommended workarounds. While most TypeScript build errors have been suppressed, the  underlying runtime error related to requiredExtensions surfaced, pointing to an issue in how the  editor schema is processed at runtime.  2. Incident Timeline & Issues Encountered:  Initial State: Project using BlockNote, decision made to enhance image block functionality.  Issue 1: Next.js 15 Build Error (ParamCheck<RouteContext>)  Description: Upon upgrading or working with Next.js 15.3.2, npm run build failed with a  ParamCheck<RouteContext> TypeScript error, indicating params for API routes were expected  to be Promise-like.

original_content_blocks.content: Resolution: The src/app/api/images/[...gcsPath]/route.ts (and other API routes) were updated to  correctly type and await context.params, aligning with Next.js 15 standards. This resolved the  initial build blocker.  Issue 2: Prisma Client Type Errors  Description: Intermittent TypeScript errors related to Prisma types (e.g., Namespace '...Prisma'  has no exported member 'K').  Resolution: Resolved by running npx prisma generate to ensure the client was up-to-date.  Issue 3: BlockNote Custom Schema - BlockSpec vs. BlockConfig Type Mismatch (Lead-up to  Runtime Error)  Description: This became the most persistent and complex issue. The goal was to customize  the "image" block to support local uploads, storing metadata like GCS paths, content types, and  app-served URLs ('data-gcs-path', contentType, 'data-app-served-url'). This required defining  customImageProps and a customImageConfig (or customImageSpec).  Why BlockSpec and BlockConfig became relevant:  BlockNote's schema is defined by BlockSpec objects for each block type. A BlockSpec includes  the block's type, propSchema, content model, styling, and crucially, its underlying Tiptap  configuration (including requiredExtensions).  However, the BlockNoteSchema.create({ blockSpecs: ... }) function's blockSpecs parameter is  typed to expect a Record<string, BlockConfig>.  BlockConfig is a more minimal representation of a block's schema shape, primarily type,  propSchema, content.  A key finding (from developer discussions) is that BlockSpec is not directly or always assignable  to BlockConfig in TypeScript's structural typing, particularly when used in Record types. This is  because BlockSpec might have more properties or a slightly different structure than what  BlockConfig strictly defines for assignability.  Manifestation: This mismatch led to a cascade of TypeScript errors when:  Passing defaultBlockSpecs (which is Record<string, BlockSpec>) or our editorBlockSpecs  (containing our customImageSpec) to BlockNoteSchema.create().  Using typeof customSchema (the schema instance) as a generic argument for  BlockNoteEditor<typeof customSchema>, Block<typeof customSchema, "blockName">, etc.  These errors often stated Type 'BlockSpecs' is not assignable to 'Record<string, BlockConfig>'  or that BlockNoteSchema<...> didn't satisfy constraints expecting an index signature.  Issue 4: Runtime Error - TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading  'requiredExtensions')  Description: After numerous attempts to satisfy TypeScript using various schema definition  strategies and type suppressions for BlockNote components, this runtime error emerged during  npm run dev when initializing the editor.  Probable Cause (linked to Issue 3): This error strongly suggests that, despite our best efforts to  type the schema correctly for BlockNoteSchema.create(), the resulting compiled schema (or a  specific block config within it, likely the customized "image" block) is malformed or incomplete at  runtime from BlockNote/Tiptap's perspective. It's trying to find Tiptap extension information for a  block and encountering an undefined where it expects an object with requiredExtensions. This  often happens if a block's configuration is not properly processed or inherited.  3. Root Cause Analysis (Focus on requiredExtensions error):

The requiredExtensions runtime error likely stems from an improperly constituted BlockConfig  for the "image" block (or potentially another block if defaults were affected) within the  blockConfigs object passed to BlockNoteSchema.create(). Even if TypeScript was eventually  satisfied by casts or structural changes, the JavaScript object at runtime might be missing data  that BlockNote's core needs to set up its Tiptap extensions.  This could happen if:  The process of spreading defaultBlockSpecs.image.config.propSchema and then  adding/overriding with customImageProps resulted in a propSchema that was subtly  incompatible or incomplete.  When constructing customImageConfig, essential fields from defaultBlockSpecs.image.config  (beyond just propSchema, content, type, styleSchema like allowsBlocks or other internal fields  Tiptap relies on for its requiredExtensions setup) were not correctly carried over or were  overridden in a way that broke the chain.  The interaction with the uploadFile handler and its expected props return for image blocks might  have influenced how the "image" block was internally configured or updated, leading to this  state.  The project's ambition to create a rich image upload experience with custom metadata (GCS  paths, app-served URLs, content types) pushed the boundaries of customizing a default  BlockNote block. This involved defining new props and managing their state through the upload  lifecycle (blob URLs to permanent URLs). If this custom prop schema (customImageProps) and  its integration into the overall customImageConfig wasn't perfectly aligned with all of BlockNote's  internal expectations for an "image" block (especially one that usually handles file uploads itself  via uploadFile), it could lead to the requiredExtensions issue.  4. Remediation Steps Attempted:  Next.js 15 params Fix: Successfully implemented.  Prisma Client Regeneration: Successfully addressed Prisma type errors.  BlockNote Package Updates: Updated @blocknote/* from 0.29.1 to 0.30.0. This resolved some  TypeScript errors (evidenced by "unused @ts-expect-error" messages appearing), but not the  fundamental BlockSpec/BlockConfig assignability issues or the final runtime error.  Schema Refactoring (Extensive):  Initially tried various ways to type customImageSpec and editorBlockSpecs.  Adopted community suggestion to create a blockConfigs: Record<string, BlockConfig> by  mapping spec.config from defaultBlockSpecs and constructing customImageConfig explicitly as  a BlockConfig. This was applied to src/lib/editor/blocks.tsx.  Type Safety Restoration Attempts:  Tried using schema-derived types (typeof customSchema.BlockNoteEditor, etc.) as per  community suggestions. This led to errors like "CustomBlock is not generic" or re-exposed the  underlying BlockSchema<BlockSchemaFromSpecs<BlockSpecs>> vs Record<string,  BlockConfig> constraint violations.  Attempted explicit schema typing for customSchema using BlockSchemaFromSpecs.  Targeted Type Suppressions:  Used any casts for initialContent in useCreateBlockNote, editor in onEditorReady callback, for  CustomImageBlock type in ImageBlock.tsx, and for testProps in ImageBlock.tsx.

Used @ts-expect-error for the <BlockNoteView /> component invocation due to persistent prop  type errors.  Defensive Coding in Schema Creation: Added checks for spec.config and  defaultBlockSpecs.image.config before access in src/lib/editor/blocks.tsx to prevent errors if  these were undefined (this was done just before the runtime error appeared consistently).  5. Current Status:  The Next.js 15 ParamCheck error is resolved.  Prisma type errors are resolved.  BlockNote packages are updated to v0.30.0.  The schema creation in src/lib/editor/blocks.tsx has been refactored to build a Record<string,  BlockConfig> by using spec.config from defaults and an explicitly defined customImageConfig:  BlockConfig.  Most TypeScript strict type errors related to BlockNote generics have been worked around by:  Using non-schema-specific types in consuming components (page.tsx, ImageBlock.tsx).  Applying specific any casts in BlockNoteEditor.tsx (initialContent, onEditorReady parameter).  Applying @ts-expect-error to the <BlockNoteView /> component in BlockNoteEditor.tsx.  The application now fails at runtime during npm run dev with TypeError: Cannot read properties  of undefined (reading 'requiredExtensions') when initializing the BlockNote editor, specifically  when useCreateBlockNote is called. This error persists even after the schema creation refactor  and defensive coding in blocks.tsx.  6. Impact:  The application is currently unusable in development (npm run dev) due to the runtime error,  blocking further development and testing of features involving the BlockNote editor.  Builds (npm run build) would also fail at the same point if the runtime initialization were part of  the build check, or would produce a non-functional editor.  7. Next Steps / Recommendations for Investigation:  Isolate the Problematic Block Config:  Temporarily simplify blockConfigs in src/lib/editor/blocks.tsx. Start by only including  defaultBlockSpecs.image.config (without any custom overrides) and see if the runtime error  persists.  If that works, incrementally add back parts of your customImageConfig (especially  customImageProps) to see which part triggers the requiredExtensions error. Pay close attention  to how propSchema is constructed and merged.  Examine uploadFile Interaction (as discussed previously):  Temporarily remove the uploadFile: handleFileUploadOptimistic option from  useCreateBlockNote in BlockNoteEditor.tsx. If the runtime error disappears, the issue is highly  concentrated in how the custom image upload behavior and its associated props interact with  the "image" block's fundamental setup.  If this is the case, consider if the props returned by uploadFile need to be simpler, or if the  custom props ('data-gcs-path', etc.) should be added to the block via a separate  editor.updateBlock call after the initial block insertion by uploadFile, rather than being part of the  direct uploadFile return props that define the block from the outset.  Alternative Custom Block Strategy:

Consider creating a new, entirely separate custom block type (e.g., "myUploadedImage")  specifically for locally uploaded images, leaving the default "image" block configuration as  pristine as possible (for URL embeds). This new block would have its own BlockConfig defined  from scratch with only the necessary props (url (permanent), alt, gcsPath, contentType). This  decouples your upload logic from the potentially sensitive default "image" block.  Consult BlockNote Community/Issues with Minimal Reproduction: Provide the exact structure of  your customImageConfig and how customSchema is created. The requiredExtensions error is  specific enough that they might recognize the pattern if it's tied to a common misconfiguration of  a block that requires Tiptap extensions.
